correctness.rationale: Full 1441-face enumeration with f-vector (27,219,613,510,72), certified 662-pair acyclic discrete-Morse matching (4677 incidences), critical cells 1 in degree zero, 49 in degree two and 67 in degree three, signed integer 49-by-67 Morse boundary of rational rank 19 with a verified maximal minor determinant 1. Smith factors all units and π2 classification of attachments to a simply connected 2-skeleton yield a wedge of 30 2-spheres and 48 3-spheres. Independent mod-two ranks corroborate face and homology dimensions.

evidence: Engström https://arxiv.org/html/math/0512420v1 gives broad bounds for claw-free independence complexes.
Outerplanar theorem https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04601v2 needs outerplanarity, contradicted by 27>19 edges.
Manifold classification https://arxiv.org/html/1906.03328v3 requires manifold matching complexes, whereas this complex is nonpure.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general published theorems do not imply the exact two-degree sphere multiplicities. The most relevant wedge theorem has strictly narrower graph-class hypotheses; the manifold theorem has false hypotheses for this complex.

value.rationale: The Goldner–Harary graph is a canonical smallest non-Hamiltonian maximal planar graph, a natural test case lying outside the outerplanar matching-complex sphere-wedge theorem. Its complete integral mixed-dimensional homotopy decomposition is neither a routine consequence of general connectivity bounds nor a renaming of existing results; exact attaching-map and multiplicity data are useful concrete invariants for the planar matching-complex question. No broader theorem is asserted.
